reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the Genesis list as naming founders of clans, so Bela's sons Naaman and Ard could be counted among Benjamin's "sons."

discrepancy.connective: Critical scholar Steven DiMattei treats the two lists as genuinely divergent traditions, arguing the variations reflect editorial reworking rather than a single reconcilable genealogy.

skeptic.name: Steven DiMattei
skeptic.work: Genesis 1 and the Creationism Debate / contradictionsinthebible.com (entry #301)
skeptic.attribution: Steven DiMattei, contradictionsinthebible.com, "Were Ard and Naaman sons of Benjamin OR sons of Benjamin's son Bela?" (#301)

excerpts.excerpt_text: according to Num 26:40, two of the sons of Benjamin mentioned in Gen 46:21, Naaman and Ard, were his grandsons, sons of Belah … The two grandsons of Benjamin could be reckoned among his sons in our list, because they founded independent families just like the sons.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names Naaman and Ard explicitly and states the exact tension (sons in Gen 46:21 vs. grandsons/sons of Bela in Num 26:40), then gives the founders-of-families harmonization. Directly on-tension.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Genesis 46:8
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Treats this passage directly: names Naaman and Ard and harmonizes the son/grandson difference by reading the Genesis list as enrolling clan-founders, whether born before or after the migration to Egypt.
